newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Biota inflenza drug trial to start May.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Biota inflenza drug trial to start May.

text.p: Biotechnology company Biota Holdings Ltd said on Monday that phase three clinical trials for its anti-influenza drug, zanamirvir, or GG167, would begin in Australia in May.
Biota said it had been informed about the trial's start date by its development partner, Glaxo Wellcome Plc.

"This Southern Hemisphere trial trial will be a part of a comprehensive world-wide phase three programme which will also include two seperate pivotal proof of efficacy studies to be initiated in the Northern Hemisphere from October of this year," the company said in a statement.

Biota said results from the phase IIB studies from the Northern Hemisphere together with earlier studies confirmed that zanamivir was a potentially valuable therepy for influenza and said data from these studies allowed for the optimisation of the phase three programme.

The company said concurrent with the phase three programme, it would in collaboration with U.S. company Biostar Inc, continue to develop and commercialise a rapid and easy-to-use diagnostic aid for influenza.
"World-wide filing for zanamivir is planned to take place in the second half of 1998," the company said.
Biota said the drug would be administered twice daily for five days in the phase three trials using Glaxo Wellcome's Diskhaler technology for inhaled dosing directly into the lungs.
The company said it estimated that there were more than 350 million cases of inflenza around the world each year.
"In the U.S., influenza and its complications represent the sixth leading cause of death," Biota said.
